$comment: Size ceilings (bytes) for the SHIPPED studio build, checked by scripts/check-bundle-budget.ts in test.yml's gated `studio-dist` job, after a real `bun run build`. Studio is a dev tool so end users do not download it, but it is otherwise unmonitored (the codecov bundle path is broken — see codecov-bundle-analysis-diagnosis.md). Raise a ceiling deliberately, with justification, when a real feature grows it. A directory key budgets its whole tree minus source maps.
$ratchet: monaco-editor 0.55.1 -> 0.56.0 moved the metafile build 14202972 -> 14572625 bytes (+369653, +2.6%), and the split release build 13822091 -> 14189667 over the same change. The old 14000000 ceiling was already being met on tolerance rather than under the ceiling (main sat at 101.4%), which is how a real 2.6% growth would have been absorbed silently. Raised deliberately to just above the measured figure so the next regression has to be argued for.
$ratchet-kit-coexistence: The UI kit joined the startup path (registerKit(): its component documents, the Phosphor manifest for the ~100 glyphs the shell uses, and the theme sheet) while Spectrum stays registered until the last lit surface migrates, moving studio.js 2931123 -> 3032009 (+100886, +3.4%), on tolerance against the 3000000 ceiling. Raised to just above the measured figure for the coexistence period; it comes back DOWN in the removal PR, when the 36 Spectrum packages leave. The keyed-list reconciler and mount() in the runtime moved iframe-entry.js 266632 -> 278364 (+11732, +4.4%) on the same rule.
$was-measuring-the-wrong-thing: Until now the only budgeted key was studio.js at 14600000, and it was checked on the bundle-analysis lane after `bun run build:metafile` — a single unsplit `bun build` with no splitting and no shared contract, which inlines Monaco and everything else. That lane wrote its output to dist/ too, so it OVERWROTE the release build's studio.js at the same path. The artifact that actually ships is 2.93 MB, five times smaller, and had no ceiling at all; neither did iframe-entry.js, chunks/ or workers/. The metafile lane writes to dist-metafile/ now and the budgets below are measured from `bun run build`.
$ratchet-iframe-entry: Change highlighting (git-diff artboards) added DIFF_MARK_CSS, syncDiffCss and applyDiffMarks to iframe-render.ts, moving iframe-entry.js 257959 -> 260075 bytes (+2116, +0.8%). The old 260000 ceiling was then being met on TOLERANCE rather than under the ceiling (100.0%), which is the exact shape the studio.js note below warns about: the next real growth would be absorbed silently. Raised to just above the measured figure so it has to be argued for instead. Then browser verification split a modification into the two faces it wears (red on the committed side, green on the working copy — marked identically it read as 'added' over the very text being replaced), which is one more CSS rule: 260075 -> 266632, and 101.8% of the 262000 set above. Raised again to just above the measured figure, on the same rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-iframe-entry-dialogs: Dialogs shown in place (studio.md §4.2.3) added the dialog rules, applyCanvasDialogOpen, the setDialogOpen and redefineElement handlers and the commandTargetClick report to the frame, moving iframe-entry.js 279541 -> 284792 bytes (+5251, +1.9%) — over the 280000 ceiling and onto the tolerance, which is the shape every note in this file warns about. Raised to just above the measured figure, on the same rule.
$ratchet-spectrum-removal: The $ratchet-kit-coexistence note above promised this and it came due: the 36 @spectrum-web-components entries (50 resolved, plus colorjs.io, @lit-labs/virtualizer and lit itself, which nothing imported once the two LitElement selectors went) left packages/studio, and with them the registry, the brand fragment and styles/spectrum.css. studio.js 4140570 -> 2640946 bytes (-1499624, -36.2%), so the 3040000 ceiling comes back DOWN to 2700000 — just above the measured figure, on this file's own rule, and below both figures the coexistence note cites (3032009 during coexistence, 2931123 before the kit). That prediction was right about the direction and wrong about the size, in the honest direction: it expected a return to roughly the pre-kit 2.93 MB, and the shipped bundle is 290177 bytes UNDER that, because the kit weighs less than the lit templates and Spectrum classes it replaced. chunks goes 12500000 -> 12900000, and that RAISE is the one number here that grows. It is justified rather than convenient: the measured figure is 12752619, which is over the old ceiling and reaches green only through the 5% tolerance — the shape every note in this file warns about — and the ceiling was already unmet before this change, because Spectrum was only about 590 KB of that tree. iframe-entry.js 290788 -> 289726 and workers 13617430 -> 13617430, byte-identical, which is what says the before and after are measurements of the same tree.
$measure-with-no-dev-server-running: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING A NUMBER FROM THIS FILE. `scripts/check-bundle-budget.ts` measures whatever is in `dist/`, and `bun run build` wipes that directory first — so the figures above are clean by construction, but only if nothing else is writing there. A `bun run dev` watcher is: it rebuilds the studio bundle on save, into the same `dist/`, AFTER the wipe and without one of its own, so its output accumulates beside the release build's under different chunk hashes. Measured on the Spectrum-removal branch: with a dev server up, chunks reported 25498884 bytes and the gate failed at 197.7%; the very next `bun run build` with the server stopped reported 12752619 across 107 chunks, with ZERO byte-identical duplicates under a hash- and debugId-normalising comparison. Same commit, same command, twice the bytes. That is worth writing down because it has already misled once: the §C8 survey measured 25977090 across 267 files and attributed 8922445 of it to the two-pass build emitting shared chunks twice, including two Monaco chunks of 5086021 and 5082169 differing in four lines — which is exactly the shape a stale watcher leaves behind, and which one clean rebuild does not reproduce. Treat the duplicate-chunk finding as unproven rather than as fixed by anything in this change: nothing here touched the build's splitting.
$ratchet-iframe-entry-c8: C8 moved iframe-entry.js DOWN, 290788 -> 289726 bytes, and it is still 101.3% of the 286000 ceiling — green only on TOLERANCE, which is the exact shape every note above warns about: the next real growth would be absorbed silently. C8 did not cause the overrun (the canvas realm gained the keyed reconciler, mount() and the dialog transposition across A1/A2/A5) and it is not this slice's to explain, but leaving a key on tolerance because the number improved is how a budget stops budgeting. Raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's own standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-kit-loaders: The canvas frame registers the kit's behaviour sidecars as LAZY loaders (embedding.md §6, ui.md §10): a project on the canvas that uses a kit element names its sidecar by `jx-ui:` specifier, which nothing served, so every kit element with a behaviour failed to mount there (measured on stylebook/jx-combobox.json: ten elements, none reaching its control). The fix is a table of twenty-two `import()` thunks in iframe-entry.ts, one chunk per module on first use, so a page that draws no kit element loads none of them. Measured on a clean `bun run build` with the watcher stopped: iframe-entry.js 290146 -> 292918 (+2772, +1.0%, the table and the preloadModule import) and chunks 12860026 -> 13004222 (+144196, +1.1%: twenty-two behaviour chunks, the largest icons at 47615 because it carries the glyph manifest, and the shared pieces the splitter lifted out of studio.js, which moved 2649372 -> 2652418). Both keys were on tolerance afterwards (100.3% and 100.8%), which is the shape every note in this file warns about, so both are raised to just above the measured figure on the file's own standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance. The eager alternative — seeding all twenty into the entry — was measured at 46024 bytes minified before this was chosen, and rejected because the frame renders whatever project is open and most projects draw no kit element at all.
$ratchet-grid-lazy-chunk: grid-view.ts (and the tabulator-tables import it carries, CSS included) moved from a static import inside grid-panel.ts to a memoized dynamic import (grid-lazy.ts), for the same reason Monaco is lazy — tabulator-tables 6.5.3's Row class started running document.createElement in a static field, so a static value-import made grid-panel.ts, and therefore app-commands.ts's command set, unsafe to load from a bare Bun process. Measured on a clean `bun run build` with the watcher stopped: studio.js 2623277 -> 2130501 bytes (-492776, -18.8%: the whole grid engine left the entry bundle) and chunks 13002064 -> 13746645 (+744581, +5.7%: the engine's own chunk, its CSS chunk, and the shared pieces the splitter lifted out of studio.js with it) — over the 13050000 ceiling and onto the tolerance, which is the shape every note in this file warns about. Raised to 13900000, just above the measured figure, on the file's own standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-jxn: Jx Notation (spec.md §22) brought @bgotink/kdl into Studio, by design: reading and writing .jxn in process needs no host. The canvas first imported the parser statically, which moved iframe-entry.js to 210725 bytes; it now loads it when a .jxn reference turns up, leaving 160744 bytes, the seam and its message over the old ceiling's tolerance. The lazily loaded parser is what moved chunks to 8323126. Both measured after a real `bun run build` with no dev server running.
$ratchet-insert-panel: The persistent Insert panel (studio.md §5.3) measured against main at its merge base, both after a clean `bun run build` with no dev server running: iframe-entry.js 160991 -> 161891 (+900, the frame resolving a drop on blank canvas to the nearest edge of the root's blocks, layout pages included) and chunks 8388893 -> 8398050 (+9157, the English element catalog and the tabbed palette surface), with studio.js 1062559 -> 1066783 (+4224) under its ceiling. Main already met both keys on TOLERANCE (104.5% and 104.9%), the shape every note in this file warns about, and this change pushed iframe-entry.js past it. Both are raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-review-changes: Review changes drawing the picked change's comparison in its centre (studio.md §22.8: the friendly change list, the stage's review layout and the Publish document's regions) measured against main at its merge base, both after a clean `bun run build` with no dev server running: chunks 8402592 -> 8416008 (+13416) and studio.js 1067306 -> 1077487 (+10181), with iframe-entry.js unchanged at 161891 and workers unchanged. Main already met chunks on TOLERANCE (100.0% of 8400000), the shape every note in this file warns about; raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-collection-page-preview: A collection's page previewed with a real entry (studio.md §4.1, §22.4: entry-bound text drawn live and badged, the stamper leaving an entry's body unaddressed, and the entry-preview bar) measured against main at its merge base, both after a clean `bun run build` with no dev server running: iframe-entry.js 161891 -> 164608 (+2717, the entry-binding rules the frame's edit-mode walk and its text patcher now run), chunks 8526390 -> 8528600 (+2210, the bar's surface document) and studio.js 982031 -> 988447 (+6416) under its ceiling, workers unchanged. iframe-entry.js left its ceiling for the tolerance with this change, and main already met chunks on TOLERANCE (101.3% of 8420000), the shape every note in this file warns about; both are raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-entry-in-page: An entry written inside its collection's page (studio.md §22.5: the field typed in place, its nested editing host in the frame, and the entryState message that replaces the page's live entry without a redraw) measured against main at its merge base, both after a clean `bun run build` with no dev server running: iframe-entry.js 164660 -> 165657 (+997), chunks 8531681 -> 8533915 (+2234) and studio.js 988497 -> 988894 (+397), both under their ceilings, workers unchanged. iframe-entry.js left its ceiling for the tolerance (100.4% of 165000), the shape every note in this file warns about; raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-minify: Release bundles are minified now (studio.md §11.1: `studioReleaseOptions` in scripts/build-config.ts, spread by scripts/build.ts into both entry passes and passed to the three Monaco worker builds; the dev watcher is NOT minified). Every key comes DOWN, to just above the new measured figure, on this file's standing rule. Measured as clean builds of one tree, each a `rm -rf dist && bun run build` with no watcher writing there, before -> minified: studio.js 2173855 -> 1108372 (-49.0%), iframe-entry.js 299357 -> 153193 (-48.8%), chunks 14174366 -> 7837093 (-44.7%), workers 13615336 -> 7859138 (-42.3%). The ceilings are set from the $ratchet-production-define note's figures, because that is the build that ships; this step is recorded on its own so the two changes can be judged, and reverted, apart. Worth recording: the 'before' column was already on TOLERANCE for two keys — iframe-entry.js at 101.8% of 294000 and chunks at 102.0% of 13900000 on main — which is the shape every note above warns about; this change did not cause that and halves it away rather than explaining it. Two consequences for the next person to measure. The dev watcher's output is now about twice the release build's for the same source, so the $measure-with-no-dev-server-running warning above applies with more force: a watcher-written dist/ now fails EVERY key, not just chunks. And Bun 1.4.2 ignores minify.keepNames (it emits byte-identical output with and without it; measured here as under 1 KB of difference across the whole tree), so a dependency that dispatches on a function or class name would break only in this build — build-config.ts records the survey that says nothing does today. The workers gained linked maps with this change (about 21 MB, 17.9 MB of it ts.worker.js.map) and they are kept, for the same reason the entries keep theirs; they are outside every key here because a directory key excludes maps, and outside the npm tarball because package.json lists dist/workers/*.js rather than the directory, which check-studio-package.ts rule 5 now enforces. Publishing the directory whole, as it was, would have shipped them and more than doubled the worker share of the tarball (13.6 MB -> 29 MB) with this gate green.
$ratchet-production-define: The release build's entry passes define process.env.NODE_ENV as "production" (`studioReleaseDefine`, studio.md §11.1), measured on top of the $ratchet-minify step, on the same tree by the same procedure, minified -> minified + NODE_ENV: studio.js 1108372 -> 1079992 (-28380, -2.6%, which is the development build of @vue/reactivity leaving: its [Vue warn] reporter and the scope/effect misuse checks), iframe-entry.js 153193 -> 151331 (-1862, -1.2%), chunks 7837093 -> 7828546 (-8547, -0.1%: the chunk tree carries the CSS chunks, which the define cannot touch), workers 7859138 -> 7859138 (Monaco reads no NODE_ENV, so the workers do not take the define and are byte-identical across this step, which is what says the two measurements are of the same tree). Overall, before minification -> now: studio.js -50.3%, iframe-entry.js -49.4%, chunks -44.8%, workers -42.3%. Ceilings, set from these figures: studio.js 2700000 -> 1100000, iframe-entry.js 294000 -> 153000, chunks 13900000 -> 7900000, workers 14000000 -> 7900000. If the minify step ever stands without this define (the define reverted, or the two changes landed as separate commits), studio.js sits at 100.8% and iframe-entry.js at 100.1% of those ceilings, on tolerance, so that tree must raise those two to just above the $ratchet-minify figures (1110000 and 154000), on this file's standing rule.
$ratchet-body-eraser: TypeScript function bodies in the canvas (spec.md §23.1, embedding.md §6.2) brought @jxsuite/erase/browser into Studio, by design: the stripper carries a TypeScript compiler, and a body has to be erased before the canvas can run it. The canvas first imported it statically, which moved iframe-entry.js to 3861402 bytes; it now loads it as its own chunk the first time a rendered document has a body that needs it, so a project with no typed body never downloads it. Measured after a clean `bun run build` with no dev server running: iframe-entry.js 165657 -> 167619 (+1962, the loader and the seam) and chunks 8622328 -> 12270614 (the eraser's chunk, the TypeScript compiler almost all of it). Both raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-live-text: Bound text drawn as its value on the editing canvas (studio.md §4.5, §6.9, §8.2.7) moved iframe-entry.js 167619 -> 196805 bytes (+29186, +17.4%), measured by the studio-dist job's own clean `bun run build`. It is the feature's weight and not a stray import: the frame now carries the chip model and the tag reader (iframe-chips.ts, @jxsuite/schema/dynamic-tag), the node stamps a commit writes back (editor/kept-node.ts), and the larger serializer, position and patch rules that keep a binding through every write, where the transform used to hand it one label string per binding. A per-module metafile of the entry shows no module that is not the canvas's own, the runtime's or the schema guards'. Raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's standing rule: under the ceiling, not on the tolerance.
$ratchet-live-rows: Every row of a repeater drawn on the editing canvas (studio.md §4.5) moved iframe-entry.js 196805 -> 206384 bytes (+9579, +4.9%), measured after a clean `bun run build`: the row view (canvas/iframe-rows.ts: active and echo rows, promotion, the union rect, the settle pass), patches that visit every instance of a path with its own row scope, and the runtime's replaceListRow. That is on the tolerance of the 198000 ceiling, the shape every note in this file warns about; raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's standing rule.
$ratchet-remote-data: Remote data fetched once on the editing canvas (studio.md §4.5) moved iframe-entry.js 206384 -> 213892 bytes (+7508, +3.6%), measured after a clean `rm -rf dist && bun run build`: the frame's answer to each remote lookup and the marks for a binding with no value (canvas/iframe-remote.ts: the per-tab store, the lookup key, the 30 second bound, the status pass over chips, bound blocks and template rows), the runtime's setRemoteLookupHandler, the status rules in the edit sheet, and the report the frame posts. Its imports are the frame's own (utils/edit-display.ts constants, canvas/iframe-rows.ts, canvas/iframe-protocol.ts) and the schema guards; nothing new is pulled in. That is on the tolerance of the 207500 ceiling, the shape every note in this file warns about; raised to just above the measured figure, on the file's standing rule.
